parties.party: BP Properties Ltd / BP Pension Trust (now BP plc)
parties.route: Letter before claim; set the 1987 judgment aside (Takhar v Gracefield, the gateway); deceit, trespass and mesne profits, unjust enrichment / account of profits; s.32 Limitation Act 1980 if concealment is shown.
Mesne profits for 1993–95 possession (trespass); unjust enrichment. An innocent purchaser for value is protected (Limitation Act 1980 s.32(3)).
Mary’s estate (Law Reform (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1934); negligence in the 1953–55 proceedings and their enforcement; s.32 if concealment is shown.
Indemnity for a register mistake (Land Registration Act 2002 Sch 8); rectification (Sch 4); Independent Complaints Reviewer (ICR/090/26).
Negligence in planning and conservation duties; Human Rights Act 1998 / A1P1 for acts after 2 Oct 2000; Public Services Ombudsman for Wales.
Negligence in the 1988 listing process; Human Rights Act 1998 / A1P1 for acts after 2 Oct 2000; Public Services Ombudsman for Wales.
Trespass to the person and misfeasance in public office (1988); IOPC complaint route.
Professional negligence; 15-year longstop (Limitation Act 1980 s.14B) unless s.32 applies.

entries.head: The farmhouse and the land (Parcel A, about 10 acres)
entries.basis: Market value today, HPI-uplifted (page 5298 Head 1). Low: existing-use value: the Vale detached-house average (£539,042, Jul 2026) plus 10 acres at £8,200/acre. Mid / high: the land share (25% / 33%) of the developed value today (20 houses × £551,929 / £605,565) plus the woodland and green at farmland rates.

entries.head: Loss of use and mesne profits, Dec 1988 – Oct 2026
entries.basis: Rental value × years since 1988: the Vale market rent (ONS, Aug 2026) back-cast year by year with the Wales HPI, summed Dec 1988 – Oct 2026 (page 5298 line 2b).

entries.head: Contents lost with the demolition
entries.basis: William’s own figure in 1989: about £30,000 (press cutting N13), taken at its 1988 value. Interest on it is in the interest head.

entries.head: Distress and psychiatric injury: William, his partner and three children
entries.basis: Judicial College Guidelines (17th ed.), psychiatric damage generally. Low: 5 × the foot of the moderate bracket. Mid: 2 adults at the middle of moderately severe + 3 children at the middle of moderate. High: 2 adults at the foot of severe + 3 children at the middle of moderately severe.

entries.head: Mary Williams: leg amputation (c.1955)
entries.basis: The family’s account: the stress of the first eviction dispute (notice 1953, order 1955) brought on the amputation. Judicial College Guidelines bracket for amputation of one leg (16th ed. +22%, the 17th ed. uplift): below-knee £112,180 – £152,260, above-knee £120,020 – £157,390. Low nil (causation not established); mid the middle of below-knee; high the top of above-knee. Causation: to be proven by medical records and expert evidence.

entries.head: Wrongful death: the estates of Mary (d. 1983) and William “Billy” Buckler (d. 1990)
entries.basis: Fatal Accidents Act 1976: the statutory bereavement award (£15,120) for William’s widow, plus two funerals at about £4,500 each today (estimate). High adds dependency for William’s partner and three children: 2/3 of an assumed £15,000 net a year × 15 years to the children’s majority, carried to 2026 £ by CPI (£359,651; earnings not on the record yet). Low nil (causation not established). Causation: to be proven.

sources.title: EV-0290 — South Wales Echo, 2 Jun 1990: “Billy died suddenly this week”

entries.head: Aggravated and exemplary damages: the 1988 eviction and demolition
entries.basis: Aggravated: £5,000 / £15,000 / £25,000 per person × 5 (Thompson v Commissioner of Police bands, indexed). Exemplary: nil low; mid the £60,000 award in Ramzan v Brookwide (2011) carried to 2026 £ by CPI (£92,570); high 15% of BP’s mid gain (£529,323), because category 2 is measured against the profit (Rookes v Barnard [1964] AC 1129).

sources.title: Thompson v Commissioner of Police [1998] QB 498 (aggravated and exemplary bands)
Ramzan v Brookwide Ltd [2011] EWCA Civ 985 (exemplary £60,000)

entries.head: Heritage and archaeological loss: the medieval farmhouse and the 1994 cemetery
entries.basis: Reinstatement premium: the cost of rebuilding a comparable historic farmhouse (250 m² at £3,500/m² mid; 300 m² at £4,500/m² high; floor area estimate) less its market value already in the land head (£539,042). Archaeology: no one owns human remains, so the 1,026 burials carry no money value; the finds (Museum Wales 95.56H) are a return-or-copy remedy in kind, £0 here.

entries.head: Costs borne by the family
entries.basis: Litigant-in-person time at £24 an hour (CPR 46.5) × 270 / 540 / 1,080 hours (page 5298 line 8a), plus £211.93 of receipted cash. The costs of the 1955, 1962, 1974 and 1986–88 proceedings: £ not on the record yet.

entries.head: Interest on the loss of use and the contents
entries.basis: Mid and high at 8% simple, the Judgments Act rate, on each year’s loss of use from when it fell due (page 5298 line 4c: £459,400 on the mid rent; scaled to the high rent) and on the £30,000 contents from Dec 1988 (37.88 years). Low at Bank Rate +1% (s.35A Senior Courts Act 1981; mean Bank Rate 4.5%). No interest on the land head: its value is already carried to today by the HPI.
